summary: The verdict links' index by claim is dropped. Nothing that verifies or serves claims read it; it was used only to find a deleted claim's own links. A deleted claim now leaves its links: a requeue that meets one drops it, and a paced sweep a day finds the rest. Measured on a copy of a real member, this gave back 2.36% of the file, about 447 bytes per signed claim.

replay.detail: No replay. A new daily task, the orphan verdict-link sweep, walks claim_verdict_links in primary-key order from a cursor in meta: 512 rows or 10 ms per writer loan, each followed by an equally long quiet interval, resuming after a restart. Measured on the copy, a full pass over 8.4M links took 379 s in 16,477 loans, longest writer hold 31 ms.

schema.detail: The index claim_candidate_verdict_links_claim_index is dropped at open and no longer created. Three meta keys are added: claim_verdict_links_sweep_link and claim_verdict_links_sweep_claim (the sweep's cursor) and claim_verdict_links_sweep_passed (when the last pass ended). No table, column, kind, digest or storage version changes; storage stays at its current version.

rules.detail: Verdicts are unchanged. Deleting a claim (a checkpoint drop, a local trim, closed-mail retirement) no longer deletes its verdict links, because without the index that would scan every link. A stale link costs at most one extra requeue of a claim that is gone, which the judge already skips. A requeue page drops the links it meets whose claim is gone, and the sweep drops the rest. A test captures every statement that deleting, requeuing, judging and sweeping run and checks with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN that none scans claim_verdict_links.

compatibility.detail: No wire, digest, capability or synced-table change: peers of any version are unaffected in both directions (measured: replication inventory digest equal before and after; fleet test with the previous release, upgrade, rollback and upgrade again).

downtime.detail: The first open after upgrading drops the index in one transaction: 631 ms on the copy, before the daemon serves. The freed pages then go back 128 per write (on the copy, 2,740 writes, p99 50 ms, max 92 ms).

manual.detail: Nothing to do. A store without incremental auto-vacuum reuses the freed pages but does not shrink (see docs/st3/retention.md).

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release is supported. Its open recreates the index (CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS) in one transaction before it serves. On the copy that took 12.3 s for 8.4M links, about 1.25 GB of index, so a rolled-back member starts that much later. Upgrading again drops it again. Links that stale deletes left behind are harmless to the previous release: it requeues the claim they name, finds it gone, and skips it.
